messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finfrontier.com>

Cc: FinFrontier Support <support@finfrontier.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:32:00 +0000
Subject: High tail-latency and 503s during peak — impact on payments

Hi Olga,

We saw a sharp spike in tail latency and repeated 503s between 14:12 and 14:20 UTC that affected payment completions for several merchants. Our monitoring shows ~12% of checkout attempts failed or timed out; we had to roll traffic to an alternate gateway to clear the backlog. Attached a screenshot of our alerts and a small sample of failed request IDs.

Can Redwood confirm whether this maps to a service disruption on your side? If eligible, we'll be requesting SLA remediation/credits — we need an outline of the impacted window and any available logs/traces to expedite internal audits.

This is high priority for our ops and payments teams.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Director, Payments Engineering
FinFrontier

Attachment: finfrontier_error_screenshot.png (png)
Attachment: failed-requests-sample.csv (csv)

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm escalating this immediately to SRE and account.

Quick ask to help us triage: can you confirm the primary affected region (us-west-2 vs us-east-1) and whether the failures were consistently 503 or mixed with increased latency/429s? Also: any sample request ids you can share (you included a CSV, but the first column looks truncated in our view) — those will let us pull traces quickly.

Marcus, Steph — looping you in to validate the window and pull traces. We will aim to provide a preliminary impact window and whether this meets SLA disruption criteria within 90 minutes.

Next steps (mutual action):
- FinFrontier: re-send 3-5 full request IDs and confirm region.
- Redwood SRE (Marcus): pull aggregate latency/5xx by shard and correlate with infra events.
- Olga/Account (me, Steph): prepare customer-facing note + estimate for credit eligibility and postmortem timeline.

I will follow up with an initial timeline and what we can provide for evidence.

Regards,

Subject: Re: High tail-latency and 503s during peak — impact on payments

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 14:45, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Marcus, Steph — looping you in to validate the window and pull traces.

Thanks, Olga. Quick summary of what I've found so far (prelim):
- Aggregate metrics show a short-lived spike in 95th/99th latency and an increase in 503 responses from 14:11:30 -> 14:19:40 UTC (approx).
- Root cause appears correlated with a shard rebalancing event triggered by an autoscaler mis-evaluation under a burst pattern; one inference pool experienced transient queue saturation and KV cache thrashing.
- Region impacted: us-west-2 (we see increased retries from customers with backends pinned to that region).

I've attached a compressed trace bundle and the per-shard 5xx counts. This is preliminary — I want to validate with the runtime logs and confirm if this meets Redwood's SLA "service unavailability" criteria (we typically require sustained unavailability for a longer window, so this may be considered a partial availability degradation).

Attachments: request-traces.zip (zip)

Immediate mitigation steps we executed:
- Drained and reprovisioned the affected pool (14:21 UTC)
- Applied a temporary autoscaler guard to prevent immediate rebalance loops
- Prioritized KV cache warmup for pinned customers (manual warmup completed at 14:29 UTC)

I'll push a short incident note and gather the raw logs; Olga, can you confirm next customer-facing language about eligibility and whether we should offer a provisional credit estimate?

- Marcus
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finfrontier.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, FinFrontier Support <support@finfrontier.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 17:19:00 +0000
Subject: Re: High tail-latency and 503s during peak — impact on payments

Alex — thanks again for the quick report and artifacts. We're confirming the overlap: Redwood telemetry and SRE traces align with the window Marcus called out (14:11:30 -> 14:19:40 UTC) and show increased 503s and timeouts for requests routed to us-west-2.

Preliminary determination: the event looks like a transient partial availability degradation caused by autoscaler-triggered rebalance and subsequent cache miss storm. While it produced visible payment failures at your end, it does not meet our contractual definition of a full "service outage" (which requires total unavailability for a sustained period). That said, given the customer impact and regulatory sensitivity around payments, we're prepared to offer a provisional prorated credit for the impacted 8.2-minute window while we finalize the precise eligible time after log reconciliation.

What we'll provide in the next 48 hours:
- Redacted trace bundle mapped to the request IDs you provide (we have an aggregated bundle attached).
- Timeline of actions taken and mitigation steps.
- A draft postmortem (target: 5 business days) with root cause and remediation plan (permanent autoscaler tweak + KV cache warming changes).
- Provisional credit calculation and how it will be applied to your billing (we will not apply the credit until logs are reconciled and you confirm acceptance).

Action items for FinFrontier: please confirm the 3–5 full request IDs and the primary merchant ids you want prioritized for trace pulls. Once we reconcile logs, we'll update the exact eligible window and share the credit amount.

Account note: Steph will own the credit/contract communication and Marcus will finalize the tech postmortem.

Thanks for your patience — we understand the severity and are moving this up the stack.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
